text: Can an oil cleanser be foamy? Yes, an oil cleanser can absolutely be foamy, but it requires a specific type of formulation known as an oil-to-foam hybrid. Here is how the chemistry breaks down and what it means for your product line: Traditional O il Cleansers (Non-Foaming) Standard oil cleansers are made entirely of oils and emulsifiers. When you massage them into dry skin, they break down sebum, makeup, and sunscreen. When you add water, the emulsifiers bind the oil to the water, turning the product into a milky texture that rinses away clean. They do not bubble or foam. O il-to-Foam Cleansers (Foaming) These are hybrid products. They contain oils to dissolve impurities, but they also include surfactants—the cleansing agents responsible for creating lather. They apply like a traditional oil, but once water is introduced, the surfactants activate and create a foamy, sudsy lather. What This Means for "æve" Because you are focusing on a highly minimalist, raw aesthetic with products featuring just 5 ingredients of pure, cold-pressed raw oils, introducing a foaming action requires a strategic choice: To stay 100% raw and pure: You will want to stick to a traditional oil cleanser. It will feel incredibly rich, sensual, and hydrating, rinsing away as a soft milk. This aligns perfectly with the "misty, dewy hydration" and "healing" essence you established in the moodboard. To create foam: You would need to add a surfactant to your ingredient list. If you want to maintain the earthy, natural brand identity, you can opt for gentle, plant-derived surfactants (like Coco-Glucoside or Decyl Glucoside derived from coconut). Both are beautiful options, but sticking to a purely non-foaming, milky oil cleanser is the most direct way to honor a strict, cold-pressed, raw-ingredient philosophy. Do both ? You can absolutely do both, and it is a brilliant way to expand the æve line while staying true to the brand's core identity.
